MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  SEPTEMBER 25, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR HUFF at 7:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present: Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  SBCCOG/SCE  ENERGY  LEADER  PARTNERSHIP  PLATINUM  RECOGNITION
  CERTIFICATE

  Marilyn Lyon, SBCCOG/SBESC presented the City with an Energy Leader
  Partnership Platinum level certificate in recognition of the City’s efforts toward
  energy conservation. Vic Nol, SCE congratulated the City on this accomplishment
  in energy conservation.

B.  PUBLIC SAFETY PRESENTATION

  MAYOR HUFF presented a Certificate of Recognition to Deputy Tami Bouse, Los
  Angeles County Sheriff’s Dept., Lomita Station in recognition of her dedicated
  public safety service to the City.

C.  WASTE MANAGEMENT “RECYCLING HERO” DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR’S FREE
  RESIDENTIAL REFUSE SERVICE – 3RD AND 4TH QUARTER

  Winning entries were: 38 Empty Saddle Lane and 61 Cypress Way.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 25, 2018
 5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
  consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
  cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
  consideration will be voted on separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE ITEMS A-I AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the City
  Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 11, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 11, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS –SEPTEMBER 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 60517 THROUGH 60546 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $257,239.59.

E.  AUGUST 2018 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  AUGUST 2018 REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 10, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 17, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

I.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 17, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 25, 2018
 6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Representatives of Cal-Water provided an update on the progress of the water reliability
construction project.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE
  MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council enter into the attached agreement with
  Pageantry Productions to provide parade management services for the Peninsula
  Holiday Parade of Lights on December 1, 2018.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Community Services Director Clark
  noted that there have been no changes to the scope of services.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE AGREEMENT WITH PAGEANTRY
  PRODUCTIONS TO PROVIDE PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE
  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS ON DECEMBER 1, 2018.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: POCKET PARK PROJECT UPDATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: (1) name the pocket park “John and Lynn
  Taber Grove” and inscribe it on a bronze plaque along with their requested poem at their
  expense; (2) direct staff and Willdan Engineering to determine which project tasks will
  be completed by each entity; and (3) review and approve the conceptual park plan.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN recognized the Taber Family’s generosity in donating
  the funds to create this park. In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN,
  Community Services Director Clark confirmed that the donation will be processed
  through the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy via a MOU between the City and
  the Land Conservancy and any excess funds will remain with the Land Conservancy.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that the COUNCIL should ensure that there
  is proper justification for this action and that a precedent isn’t being set by naming the
  park after the donor given that the City’s past practice has been to name facilities after

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 25, 2018
   individuals and public officials that have served the City or community in various
  capacities.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, Community Services Director Clark noted
  that staff reviewed the City naming policy and believes that this action is not in violation
  of the policy.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she would not object to naming the park
  for the Tabers and she believes there is justification for the action given the public
  purpose that the park will provide and that the City has taken similar action in naming
  streets. She further suggested reviewing the City’s naming policy to possibly include
  some parameters for this type of situation.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN concurred that the COUNCIL should develop policy
  to address this type of situation going forward and suggested that these types of
  decisions be brought to the COUNCIL’S attention prior to the final recommendation.
  Further discussion ensued concerning the recommendation and the proposed park.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL (1) APPROVE THE RECOMMENDATION TO NAME
  THE POCKET PARK “JOHN AND LYNN TABER GROVE” AND INSCRIBE IT ON A
  BRONZE PLAQUE WITH THE TABER’S REQUESTED POEM AT THEIR COST; (2)
  DIRECT STAFF AND WILLDAN TO DETERMINE WHICH PROJECT TASKS WILL
  BE COMPLETED BY EACH ENTITY; AND (3) APPROVED CONCEPTUAL PARK
  PLAN.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

  STAFF WAS FURTHER DIRECTED TO REVIEW THE CITY’S FACILITY NAMING
  POLICY AND BRING BACK TO THE COUNCIL FOR DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE
  MODIFICATION TO INCLUDE DONATIONS AND STREETS.

C.  COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE APPOINTMENT PROCESS FOR EXPIRING TERMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council discuss the Commission/Committee
  appointment process for expiring terms, provide direction to staff as desired and receive
  and file this report.

  City Clerk Luce provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Discussion ensued concerning the appointment/reappointment process.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested that the process for responding be as
  simple as possible so it is not a burden to the Commissioners/Committee members.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that it would be better to call the
  Commissioners/Committee members rather than sending a letter to make it more
  personal.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 25, 2018
   Further discussion ensued concerning the reappointment process.

  COUNCIL CONCURRED THAT RATHER THAN MAILING A LETTER TO CURRENT
  COMMISSIONERS/COMMITTEE  MEMBERS,  THE  MAYOR  SHOULD
  PERSONALLY CALL EACH COMMISSIONER/COMMITTEE MEMBER TO THANK
  THEM FOR THEIR SERVICE AND INQUIRE AS TO THEIR INTEREST IN BEING
  REAPPOINTED.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  THE REPORT WAS RECEIVED AND FILED.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  AUTHORIZATION FOR CITY MANAGER TO APPROVE OPERATIONAL ENTRY GATES AND
  OPERATING PROTOCOL FOR CHANDLER RANCH AND ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB
  PROJECT. APPLICANT: THE CHADMAR GROUP AND ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB;
  LOCATION: 1 CHANDLER RANCH ROAD

  Recommendation: That the City Council: (1) authorize the City Manager to approve the
  operational entry gates as a minor modification to the project subject to approval of zone
  clearance and issuance of applicable building and electrical permits; and (2) authorize
  the City Manager to execute the Operating Memorandum, all in a form to the satisfaction
  of the City Attorney.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the option of having specific
  hours for gate operation, Planning Director Wahba commented that staff did consider
  that option, but recognizing the difficulty in enforcing such parameters that option was
  abandoned.

  Discussion ensued concerning the proposed operating protocol including the
  parameters for defining nuisance situations where the gates may be closed temporarily
  and the process for making changes to the protocol when necessary.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL (1) AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO APPROVE
  THE OPERATIONAL ENTRY GATES AS A MINOR MODIFICATION FO THE
  PROJECT SUBJECT TO APPROVAL OF ZONE CLEARANCE AND ISSUANCE OF
  APPLICABLE BUILDING AND ELECTRICAL PERMITS; AND (2) AUTHORIZE THE
  CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE THE OPERATING MEMORANDUM, ALL IN A
  FORM TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 25, 2018
 11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information
  and reports to other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities
  of currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their
  various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an interest,
  which are not otherwise agendized.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN updated the COUNCIL on the Clean Power Alliance opt out
rate, financial performance, power sources and staffing matters.

COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN mentioned that SCAG Executive Director Hasan Ikhrata
resigned to take a similar position at SANDAG.

COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN also mentioned that he will be attending the California
Contract Cities Fall Seminar October 5-7, noting that he and City Manager Prichard will be
giving a presentation on performance management.

At COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN’s request, Planning Director Wahba updated the
COUNCIL on the status of the General Plan update. He noted that the joint meeting with the
Planning Commission scheduled for October 9 will be rescheduled to a later date.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on
  currently pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized
  for future consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  APPOINTMENT OF PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEMBER

  MAYOR HUFF reported that the COUNCIL conducted interviews over that last few weeks
  for an appointment to the Park & Activities Commission.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she believes it would be prudent to make
  an appointment to fill the current vacancy recognizing that the COUNCIL will be
  undergoing recruitment for appointments to the expiring terms in the coming months.
  She recommended appointing Valerie Ciarolla at this time given her orientation to the
  equestrian community.

  MAYOR HUFF concurred noting that all of the applicants had excellent qualifications.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN and COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN concurred with the
  previous comments.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL MOVED, SECONDED BY COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPOINT VALERIE CIAROLLA TO SERVE ON THE
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 25, 2018
 13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE

14.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:17 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting. The next regular
  meeting of the City Council is scheduled for Tuesday, October 9, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in
  the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  Assistant City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
SEPTEMBER 25, 2018
